claims.text: The catalyst consists of approximately 16.4–16.8 nm FCC Pd cubic seeds enclosed by {100} facets.
The PtRuFeCoNi shell is approximately equiatomic, randomly mixed, metastable, FCC, and about 1.0 nm thick.
Controlled injection at 0.8 mL/hour into oleylamine/1-octadecene at 200°C produces epitaxial quinary alloy shells on Pd nanocubes.
The PtRuFeCoNi shell is {100}-terminated and has a square atomic arrangement.
The PtRuFeCoNi shell exhibits random atomic mixing and local lattice distortions.
Orbital hybridization in the multielement shell creates composition-dependent adsorption sites.
The multielement cocktail effect alters the local electronic structure of the PtRuFeCoNi shell.
Electron transfer occurs from Fe to Ru in the PtRuFeCoNi shell.
Electronic-structure changes and lattice distortions tune hydrogen-intermediate adsorption free energies toward thermoneutral values.
Near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption enhances HER kinetics.
Near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption enhances HOR kinetics.
The disordered PtRuFeCoNi shell maintains structural stability at low electrocatalytic temperatures, thereby promoting durability.
PtRuFeCoNi will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than commercial Pt/C and the other quinary shells.
PtRuFeCoNi will undergo less performance loss during durability cycling than commercial Pt/C and the other quinary shells.
Operando measurements will show potential-dependent active-site changes consistent with optimal hydrogen adsorption energies.
The proposed mechanism applies below approximately 80°C because the metastable disordered shell is maintained in that regime.
Heating to 300–500°C causes L10 or L12 ordering and eventual phase separation.
Thermally induced ordering or phase separation changes the active-site structure and invalidates the low-temperature catalytic mechanism.
